item.title: Colombia: At least 13 people dead, multiple injured in helicopter crash, bombing
item.description: Colombia experienced a surge of violence as a police helicopter was downed in Antioquia during a coca eradication operation, resulting in the death of eight officers. Simultaneously, a car bomb exploded outside a military aviation school in Cali, claiming five lives and injuring over thirty.

item.title: SC greenlights Trump’s NIH cuts: Impacts $783M in DEI grants; critics raise alarm
item.description: The US Supreme Court permitted the Trump administration to proceed with slashing research grants. These grants were awarded by the National Institutes of Health. The grants were aligned with diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives. The court's decision marks a significant development in a legal battle. The battle is over federal funding priorities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Unlawful appointment’: Federal judge rules Alina Habba serving illegally; acting US attorney for NJ removed
item.description: A US federal judge has ruled that Alina Habba, Donald Trump's former lawyer, was unlawfully serving as acting US attorney for New Jersey, as her interim period expired in July. Judge Matthew Brann's decision disqualifies Habba from ongoing cases, potentially voiding actions taken since July 1. The ruling, challenged by criminal defendants, halted legal proceedings.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump’s $500 million fraud fine axed: NY appeals court cites excessive penalty; injunctions remain intact
item.description: A New York appeals court overturned the $500 million civil fraud penalty against Donald Trump, deeming it excessive under the Eighth Amendment. While upholding non-financial sanctions, the court found the penalty unconstitutionally large. Eric Trump hailed the decision as a "total victory," but both sides retain the option to appeal the ruling.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump admin reviewing 55 million visas: Focus on deportable offences; 6,000 student visas already revoked
item.description: The US State Department is reviewing over 55 million visa holders. This is part of a broader vetting initiative. The aim is to identify grounds for visa revocation and deportation. The review includes social media and law enforcement records. It also includes violations of US laws. The department has revoked many visas since Trump's return.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: DC under federal control: Trump to patrol Washington streets with police, military; intensifies crackdown
item.description: President Trump announced plans to join law enforcement and National Guard personnel on patrol in Washington, D.C., amidst increased federal efforts to address crime. This announcement follows a visit by Vice President Vance and other officials to Union Station, where they served burgers to troops, an event disrupted by protesters.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Russia's biggest wave of strikes on Ukraine: US factory hit, Ukraine says Putin has no interest in peace
item.description: A Russian missile hit an American factory in Mukachevo, Ukraine. The attack injured fifteen people. It was part of a large Russian airstrike. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the factory made household items. The strike occurred during US-led peace talks. Oleksandr Merezhko wants Ukraine to join NATO. Russia opposes Western military presence. Both countries have opposing views.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ex-Trump aide back at NSA: Joe Francescon named deputy director; no senate nod needed
item.description: Joe Francescon, a former Trump administration official, is the new deputy director at the National Security Agency. This follows a leadership change including the dismissal of Wendy Noble and General Timothy Haugh. Tulsi Gabbard and Pete Hegseth praised Francescon's experience. Francescon previously worked at the NSA, Pentagon, and National Security Council. He expressed excitement to return to the NSA.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pope Leo XIV likely to visit Lebanon this year: First foreign trip as pontiff; peace in focus
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is considering a visit to Lebanon, potentially his first foreign trip as Pope, to address challenges in the Middle East and support Christian communities. Cardinal Rai indicated the visit could occur anytime between now and December, pending Vatican agreement. This trip could coincide with a planned visit to Turkiye for the Council of Nicaea anniversary.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Redistricting row: California top court rejects GOP plea for hold; cost, corruption claims surface
item.description: California's Supreme Court rejected a Republican petition to halt legislative action on redistricting maps, potentially leading to a November vote. Republicans, including Senators Strickland and Valladares, vowed to challenge what they call an "unconstitutional power grab." The "Election Rigging Response Act" faces debate amid cost concerns and allegations of partisan bias, prompting a call for a federal investigation by Republicans.

item.title: Extreme heatwave warning in US: Temperature could reach triple digits; which states are at risk, advisory and safety tips
item.description: A dangerous heatwave is scorching the US Southwest, impacting over 80 million people with triple-digit temperatures expected to persist through the weekend. Extreme heat warnings are in effect across multiple states, urging residents to stay hydrated and limit outdoor activity. Vulnerable populations face serious health risks, with authorities activating cooling centers and advising caution to prevent heat-related illnesses.

item.title: UAE: 377kg of crystal meth found hidden in oil cans, three asian nationals arrested in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Abu Dhabi Police, in coordination with the National Drug Control Service, seized 377kg of crystal meth hidden in sewing machine oil cans and arrested three Asian nationals. The sophisticated smuggling attempt was foiled by expert surveillance. Authorities urged public vigilance and promoted the Aman Service as a secure, confidential platform for reporting drug-related and cybercrime activities.
